threat_actors.name: StubMaker operators
threat_actors.description: The unnamed threat actor group behind the 'StubMaker' typosquatting campaign on the RubyGems repository. The group used the personas 'Riley Miller' and 'Alex Davis' to publish 16 malicious packages.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
attack_patterns.description: The campaign leveraged typosquatting on the RubyGems repository, tricking developers into installing malicious packages with names that were subtle misspellings of legitimate gems, such as 'brumdler' instead of 'bundler'.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
attack_patterns.description: A Ruby hook in the `extconf.rb` file was executed during the malicious gem's installation process to download the next stage payload from an external source.

attack_patterns.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
attack_patterns.description: The malicious Ruby script downloaded a Rust-based loader from an external source, specifically a GitHub repository.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials from Password Stores
attack_patterns.description: The Go-based infostealer payload harvested sensitive information from Chromium-based browsers, including cookies and saved passwords.

attack_patterns.name: Credentials In Files
attack_patterns.description: The infostealer was designed to collect cryptocurrency wallet files, seed phrases, and Telegram session data from files on the compromised system.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: The collected sensitive data, including credentials and wallet files, was bundled and exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled command-and-control server.

malware.name: StubMaker
malware.description: A multi-stage Windows information stealer distributed via the StubMaker campaign. It consists of a Rust-based loader that downloads and executes a Go-based stealer payload in memory. The payload is designed to harvest browser credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and Telegram session data.

tools.name: Ruby
tools.description: The Ruby interpreter and gem package manager were abused to execute a malicious hook (`extconf.rb`) during the installation of a typosquatted package, which then downloaded the next stage payload.

campaigns.name: StubMaker
campaigns.description: A software supply chain attack discovered in August 2026 that used typosquatted packages on the RubyGems repository to distribute Windows information-stealing malware.

identities.name: RubyGems
identities.description: The public package repository for the Ruby programming language, which was targeted by the StubMaker campaign through the use of typosquatted malicious packages.

identities.name: GitHub
identities.description: The code hosting platform used by the attackers to host the second-stage Rust-based loader payload.

identities.name: Telegram
identities.description: The desktop application whose session data was targeted for theft by the StubMaker infostealer.

infrastructure.name: StubMaker Payload Hosting
infrastructure.description: A GitHub repository was used to host the second-stage Rust-based loader, which was downloaded by the initial malicious Ruby script.

infrastructure.name: StubMaker C2 Server
infrastructure.description: An attacker-controlled command-and-control server used to receive exfiltrated data, including browser credentials, crypto wallets, and Telegram session data.

indicators.name: Malicious RubyGems Hook File
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Malicious RubyGems Hook File Creation
id: 2b8c1a9d-f3e4-4b1a-8c9d-1a2b3c4d5e6f
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of extconf.rb, which can be used in malicious RubyGems to execute code during installation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/16-typosquatted-rubygems-packages-steal.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\extconf.rb'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Suspicious Download from GitHub during Gem Installation
indicators.stix_pattern: [network-traffic:dst_ref.type = 'domain-name' AND network-traffic:dst_ref.value = 'raw.githubusercontent.com' AND network-traffic:src_ref.type = 'process' AND network-traffic:src_ref.name IN ('ruby.exe', 'gem.exe')]
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Suspicious Download from GitHub during Gem Installation
id: 9d8c7b6a-5f4e-4d3c-2b1a-0987654321fe
status: experimental
description: Detects network connections from ruby.exe or gem.exe to raw.githubusercontent.com, which can indicate a malicious gem downloading a next-stage payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/16-typosquatted-rubygems-packages-steal.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1105
level: high
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ruby.exe'
      - '\gem.exe'
    DestinationHostname: 'raw.githubusercontent.com'
    Initiated: true
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Installation of Typosquatted Ruby Gem 'brumdler'
indicators.pattern:
title: Installation of Typosquatted Ruby Gem 'brumdler'
id: 5a4b3c2d-1e0f-4a9b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects the installation of 'brumdler', a known typosquatted malicious RubyGem from the StubMaker campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/16-typosquatted-rubygems-packages-steal.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'gem install'
      - 'brumdler'
  condition: selection

indicators.name: Ruby Process Spawning Network Utility
indicators.pattern:
title: Ruby Process Spawning Network Utility
id: 1d2e3f4a-5b6c-4d7e-8f9a-0b1c2d3e4f5a
status: experimental
description: Detects a Ruby process spawning a network utility like powershell.exe or curl.exe, which is suspicious during package installation.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/16-typosquatted-rubygems-packages-steal.html
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1105
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\ruby.exe'
      - '\gem.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
  condition: selection
